system.name: M3U
system.one_liner: a kernel MMU plugin that scales post-copy live migration of high-end VMs via parallel, lock-reduced page-table updates

components.name: HPT Update Operations
components.role: queued HPT update operations mixed across threads, color-coded by target address region

components.name: Lock Space Partitioning
components.role: splits operations by HVA so each falls within a single pmd and is assigned to an independent worker thread (t1-t4)

components.name: HPT Update w/o Lock Contention
components.role: kernel-side page-table walk (pgd to pud to pmd) that applies each thread's updates without cross-thread lock contention

components.name: pgd
components.role: page global directory walked to reach the pud

components.name: pud
components.role: page upper directory holding per-thread, color-coded entries that fan out to separate pmd tables

components.name: pmd
components.role: page middle directory entries locked and updated independently per thread

components.name: Page Flagging
components.role: lightweight flagging mechanism that marks pmd entries as updated per thread instead of a full unmap/remap

components.name: Redundancy Refinement
components.role: merges the per-thread completion signals and eliminates redundant per-thread TLB flush and EPT callback into one refined flush

components.name: TLB flush
components.role: single aggregated TLB flush performed once all per-thread updates are done

content.key_idea: Partitioning HPT update operations across independent pmd regions and replacing per-thread unmap/TLB-flush/EPT-callback with lightweight page flagging and one aggregated flush lets M3U parallelize dirty-page registration without lock contention.
content.reading_order: Left to right: raw HPT update operations are partitioned by address region and thread (t1-t4), cross the user/kernel boundary, walk pgd/pud/pmd with page flagging per thread, then converge into one refined TLB flush.

summary: M3U reduces lock contention during parallel dirty-page registration for post-copy VM migration. This figure traces HPT update operations through three left-to-right stages. First, Lock Space Partitioning splits operations by HVA so each falls within a single pmd and is handed to an independent worker thread (t1-t4, color-coded); the dashed t4 group is used as the running example. Crossing the user/kernel boundary, operations walk the page-table hierarchy (pgd to pud to pmd); Page Flagging then marks each thread's pmd entries as updated with a lightweight lock instead of a full unmap, so the PUD/PMD locks required are independent per 1 GB region. Finally, Redundancy Refinement merges the four threads' 'Done' signals so only one aggregated TLB flush and EPT callback is performed, instead of one per thread.
